tables.name: portrait_key_light_patterns
tables.units: degrees (azimuth from camera axis toward the lit side; elevation above eye level)
rows: symmetric shadow under nose; shadow under chin
small nose-shadow loop toward mouth corner, not touching cheek shadow
nose shadow merges with cheek shadow; lit triangle under far eye
face halved along the nose line
bright edge on jaw or ear, no frontal key
tables.population: Photographic convention, not a measured dataset
tables.notes: Typical bands from portrait-lighting practice (e.g. Hunter, Biver & Fuqua, Light: Science and Magic); books differ by 5-15 degrees. Use only as an initialisation or classification aid for key direction.

tables.name: lighting_ratio_conventions
tables.population: Arithmetic from the two common definitions; not empirical
tables.notes: Def A: label = (key+fill)/fill, so stops = log2(label). Def B: label = key/fill with fill on both sides, so lit/shadow = label+1. Store stops, never the label. Commercial portraits often fall around 2:1-4:1 (Def A) by practitioner convention.

tables.name: sh_order2_irradiance_constants
tables.units: dimensionless (real spherical-harmonic basis, unit normal n = (x, y, z))
tables.notes: Irradiance E(n) = sum_lm Ahat_l * L_lm * Y_lm(n), with Ahat_0 = pi, Ahat_1 = 2pi/3, Ahat_2 = pi/4 (Ramamoorthi & Hanrahan 2001). Order 2 captures roughly 98-99% of the Lambertian kernel energy (Basri & Jacobs 2003). Dominant light direction is proportional to (L11, L1-1, L10) mapped to (x, y, z). The axis convention must match the engine's camera/world frame.

tables.name: portrait_camera_perspective
tables.units: focal length mm (35 mm-equivalent); distance m; scale ratio dimensionless
tables.population: Typical consumer and portrait practice; not a measured sample
tables.notes: near_far_scale = 1 + delta/z, the magnification of the nose tip relative to the ear plane, with delta = 0.12 m assumed (nose-tip-to-tragion depth; replace with the anthropometry note's value). Ward et al. 2018 (JAMA Facial Plastic Surgery) reported roughly 30% wider apparent nasal base at about 30 cm than at about 1.5 m (recalled; verify).

tables.name: camera_and_scale_priors
tables.population: Adults (iris, cornea); others are engineering defaults
tables.notes: Iris row confirmed 2026-11-20; engineering sigmas are not research-derived; calibrate on consented test portraits with known camera data.

tables.name: lighting_fit_defaults
rows: order-2 SH lighting model (27 for RGB)
weak prior when SH fit is ill-conditioned
tables.notes: Suggested starting values only. Exclude eyes, brows, lips, nostrils, hair and beard from the SH fit.

tables.name: verification_gate_defaults
rows: best published 300-W full-set NME ~2.9-3.3% IOD (HRNet-W18 3.32, STAR 2.87); conventions vary; corrected in verification, status: sourced
tables.population: n/a (engineering defaults and perceptual rules of thumb)
tables.notes: Never auto-accept on G3 or G4 alone; photometric and identity scores are confounded by lighting and render-vs-photo domain gap.

tables.name: blender_lens_shift_units
tables.units: divisor for pixel offset (shift = offset_px / divisor)
tables.notes: Divisors recalled from Blender source (BKE_camera_params_compute_viewplane: shift multiplied by viewfac = winx for horizontal fit). The engine forces HORIZONTAL fit but divides by max(W,H): identical for landscape, off by H/W for portrait-orientation photos. Confirm with a round-trip render test. Also recalled: the free perspective viewport applies a zoom factor of 2 (CAMERA_PARAM_ZOOM_INIT_PERSP), so viewport lens ~ 2x camera lens for the same FOV.
